chapter: Boston childhood, learning music and first gigs
title: Hodges versus Howard Johnson at Don Donaldson's rehearsals
summary: Kids listened outside Don Donaldson's house to Hodges and Howard play; Hodges had a different tone and was the Boston favorite.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: So it was a toss-up between him and Johnny, you know, who could play the best. But Johnny had a different kind of tone, a different kind of sound. Now, you could hear the two of them play the same thing, but there was a difference in Johnny's playing. And it was in the tone, you know. But the two of them together, they were really something else. A friend of mine whose name was Don Donaldson, he had an orchestra, and both of them were in the band. They used to rehearse at Don's house -- Don was a piano player. And we would stand outside in the street and listen to them play, you know.
Don Donaldson was also from Boston.

Yeah, it was still in Boston. And we'd stand outside the window and listen to... Well, we'd make comparisons between Johnny and Howard, you know. But both of them were even-up to me, at that time. But of course, Johnny had a different tone. But Johnny was the favorite. I don't know, some people just followed him, you know. Johnny was the favorite all over Boston.
